summary: Revision 4 adds a new architecture section, "Draw the system: where the judge attaches" (id=architecture), between In production and Copy these — five hand-authored inline SVG whiteboard diagrams with no external scripts or event handlers: (1) an agent loop with retrieval, tool calls, sub-agents and a trace store, marked with seven judge attachment points (J1 input check, J2 context relevance, J3 tool-call check, J4 output guardrail, J5 post-hoc response quality, J6 trajectory judge, J7 agent-as-judge), each backed by a cited legend item; (2) the three request-path topologies — inline/blocking, parallel, post-hoc/async — and what each does to p95; (3) the instrument ladder from executable check to human review plus Netflix's factuality decomposition and min() aggregation; (4) the two calibration loops; (5) the confusion matrix with the worked 200-response numbers. A pointer paragraph (production-p14) links the production cards to the drawings, a new honest caveat (architecture-p2) and a new gap (gaps-li11) record that no talk in the corpus presents a reference architecture — every box is a placement someone described in prose, cited to the sentence that justifies it. Nav, hero provenance and footer updated; guide.md mirrors the section with ASCII diagrams and [VIDEO@N] cites. Every existing id is unchanged; the only new cites are a3SMraZWNNs@9 and 8fNP4N46RRo@40, both verified verbatim against corpus/.

items.reason: Added a full diagram section with five inline-SVG architectural drawings covering exactly what was asked: an agent architecture with every place a judge can be attached (input, retrieval, tool calls, output, trajectory, agent-as-judge), the parallel-vs-inline-vs-post-hoc topology, plus the other parts of the write-up that are genuinely diagrammable (instrument ladder, calibration loops, confusion matrix). The /lavish whiteboard skill is not available on this run, so the drawings are hand-authored SVG in that style — monochrome currentColor strokes, dashed boxes for judges, no external scripts, works in light and dark. One part of the request could not be honoured from the corpus: no talk presents a reference architecture, a per-turn judge-call budget, or a rule for combining J1-J7 into one release decision, so that is recorded as a caveat (architecture-p2) and a new gap (gaps-li11) instead of being drawn from memory.
